topic_brief.title: Organic vs conventional farming crop yield gap
topic_brief.research_question: How much lower is crop yield under organic farming compared to conventional farming?
topic_brief.intervention_description: Organic farming system (certified organic or following organic principles: no synthetic fertilizers, no synthetic pesticides)
topic_brief.comparator_description: Conventional farming system (using synthetic fertilizers and/or pesticides)
topic_brief.outcome_description: Crop yield (grain, fruit, or total biomass harvested per unit area)
important_moderators: Crop type (cereal, legume, fruit, vegetable, oilseed, root/tuber)
Crop species (wheat, maize, rice, soybean, tomato, potato, etc.)
Experiment type (long-term trial, on-farm comparison, field trial)
topic_brief.benchmark_source: Ponisio et al. 2015 (Proc R Soc B 282:20141396)

rows.title: Long-term organic farming impact on soil nutrient status and grain yield at the foothill of Himalayas
rows.treatment_description: Organic: 5 t/ha FYM + 2.5 t/ha vermicompost
rows.notes: Grain micronutrient, not yield. Values from text. Fe content of organic grains almost double conventional.

rows.title: Long-term organic farming impact on soil nutrient status and grain yield at the foothill of Himalayas
rows.treatment_description: Organic: 5 t/ha FYM + 2.5 t/ha vermicompost
rows.notes: Grain micronutrient, not yield. Conventional Cu was ~5x organic. Likely due to copper-based agrochemical inputs.

rows.title: Long-term organic farming impact on soil nutrient status and grain yield at the foothill of Himalayas
rows.treatment_description: Organic: 5 t/ha FYM + 2.5 t/ha vermicompost

rows.title: Effect of organic farming practices on soil and performance of soybean (Glycine max) under semi-arid tropical conditions in Central India
rows.treatment_description: Organic farming practice (cattle dung manure on N-equivalent basis, rock phosphate for P, neem oil for pest control)
rows.control_description: Chemical/inorganic farming practice (chemical fertilizers and recommended pesticides)
rows.notes: Data is mean of 2 years (2011-2012). LSD is for management effect at P<0.05. Organic yield was HIGHER than conventional, opposite to typical yield gap literature. Soybean is a legume which may benefit more from organic N via biological fixation.

rows.title: Combined Use of Green Manure and Farmyard Manure Allows Better Nutrition of Organic Lettuce
rows.treatment_description: Green manure (GM) - common vetch incorporated into soil at flowering
rows.control_description: Conventional production system (CPS) - mineral fertilizer (80 kg N/ha, 60 kg P/ha, 60 kg K/ha)
rows.notes: Table header says 'Yield (kg/da)' but text consistently reports values as t/ha; Tukey grouping: GM=bc, Conventional=bc, not significantly different. RCB design, 3 reps, 100 m2 plots. ANOVA CV=10.7%.

rows.notes: Mean of 3 years (2003-2006). CD(5%) = 0.48 t/ha is pooled LSD. All four organic amendments combined - yield at par with chemical fertilizer (difference 0.33 t/ha < CD 0.48). This is the most complete organic system and the most relevant comparison for organic vs conventional meta-analysis.
